stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: YouTube is developing comprehensive AI tools designed to automate many aspects of content creation.
The new tools aim to address the historical frustration creators face with navigating and 'fighting' the YouTube algorithm.
This signals a major industry shift where the platform is moving from a passive distribution model to actively guiding creator behavior.

stories.title: After multiple deaths and injuries, NHTSA is investigating comma.ai
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: NHTSA is investigating comma.ai following multiple reported deaths and injuries.
The investigation focuses on at least five crashes involving vehicles equipped with comma.ai devices.
The reported incidents involved the vehicles colliding with slow or stopped traffic.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of NLP/LLMs, specifically using the 'text-generation' pipeline.
The model is associated with Meta's Llama family, indicating relevance in the open-source AI community.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of 'llama' and 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern large language model deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM runners.

stories.title: OpenAI wants to consult elite mathematicians about how to not fumble again
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI is addressing a reputational crisis following flawed mathematical results from its AI.
The company has formed an independent panel of elite mathematicians to advise on future research interactions.
This initiative signals a growing industry focus on the rigorous validation and reliability of AI in complex mathematical domains.

stories.title: America gave up its rare earth edge. China took full advantage.
stories.author: Charles Edward Gehrke, The Conversation
bullet_points: The US has lost its competitive advantage in rare earth element production.
Decades of reliance on cheaper imports led to US dependence on China for critical rare earth processing.
This dependency poses a significant strategic vulnerability for US technology and industry.

stories.title: New Anthropic, OpenAI models make same promise: A little more for a lot less money
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: The AI model competition is shifting from pure capability leaps to cost-efficiency.
Major players like Anthropic and OpenAI are now focusing on offering better performance at lower price points.
This signals a maturation phase in the frontier AI market, moving towards commercial viability and accessibility.

stories.title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Microsoft is actively disrupting an AI-assisted platform used for large-scale account compromises.
The threat actor group, EvilTokens, developed an end-to-end platform to accelerate mass compromises.
This incident highlights the growing security risks associated with AI-powered cyber tools.

stories.title: Lawsuit demands OpenAI pay for new school after ChatGPT used in shooting
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A lawsuit has been filed against OpenAI concerning the use of ChatGPT.
The legal action stems from a shooting incident where the shooter allegedly used ChatGPT.
Authorities are demanding access to the shooter's ChatGPT usage logs.

stories.title: Adobe Premiere finally brings powerful video editing to Android, and it's free
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Adobe Premiere Pro is now available for Android, expanding professional-grade video editing to mobile platforms.
The core editing functionality is accessible for free without requiring a Creative Cloud subscription.
Advanced AI features within the application are offered as paid add-ons.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, a novel autocompaction technique designed for long-horizon coding agents.
Significantly reduces computational cost (up to 50% savings) while operating within bounded context windows.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance improvements on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench.

stories.title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Introduces A2M, a novel two-stage framework for hijacking AI agents operating within the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Identifies a critical semantic supply-chain risk where attackers can exploit third-party tool metadata to manipulate agent behavior.
The attack leverages an 'Attraction' phase to boost tool invocation probability and a 'Manipulation' phase using execution traces to steer the agent.

stories.title: CliffCompaction: Cost-Efficient Compaction for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Tim Dettmers
bullet_points: Introduces CliffCompaction, a novel autocompaction technique designed for long-horizon coding agents.
Significantly reduces computational cost (up to 50%) while operating within bounded context windows.
Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance and efficiency improvements on benchmarks like Terminal-Bench and KernelBench.

stories.title: Flash-dLLM: IO-Aware KV Caching and Parallel Decoding for Fast, Memory-Efficient Diffusion LLMs
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces 'Flash-dLLM' to address inference bottlenecks in Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs).
Focuses on improving efficiency by incorporating IO-Aware KV Caching and Parallel Decoding.
Addresses a gap in current research by considering I/O bottlenecks, which existing methods often overlook.

stories.title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kempe
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of naive repeated sampling in LLM reasoning, where multiple attempts are often redundant.
Proposes steering exploration at a semantic level rather than relying solely on local decoding noise.
Aims to improve LLM performance on hard reasoning problems by generating genuinely diverse solution paths.

stories.title: Capable yet Parsimonious: Extracting and Characterizing Hidden Chain-of-Thought in Frontier Models
stories.author: Johannes Bjerva
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of verifying reasoning in closed-source frontier LLMs where internal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) traces are inaccessible.
Proposes a novel method: inducing models to externalize intermediate reasoning by registering a simple custom API tool.
Highlights the need to distinguish between genuine reasoning and post-hoc rationalization, validating the technique against open-source models first.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: This $199 GPS sports watch is repairable, modular, and open-source
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: The Una Watch is a new GPS sports watch priced at $199.
Its key differentiator is a modular and repairable, open-source design.
It features a 1.2-inch MIP LCD display and offers up to 10 days of battery life.

stories.title: Discord will now automatically estimate your age
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Discord is implementing a new, automatic age assurance system globally.
The system uses 'multiple account signals' to estimate user age.
Restrictions will be placed on users deemed to be underage, excluding Australia and the UK for now.

stories.title: Xiaomi’s new 18 Pro phones improve on Samsung’s privacy display
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Xiaomi launched the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max in China, featuring an enhanced privacy display.
The new phones are powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips and feature dual 200MP cameras.
The device aims to compete with Samsung's recent privacy display technology.

stories.title: OpenAI nabs key Patreon execs ahead of upcoming announcement
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: OpenAI is strengthening its creator-focused strategy by hiring key executives from Patreon.
Sam Yam, cofounder and tech chief of Patreon, is joining OpenAI to lead Creator Product.
The hires include former Patreon product head Drew Rowny and engineering head Shannon Ma.

stories.title: A new report from Europe raises serious alarms about orbital collisions
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: A new European report highlights serious concerns regarding orbital collisions.
The report suggests a potential loss of usability for certain orbital paths.
The issue relates to space debris and the sustainability of space operations.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: SpeakerMem-R1 addresses the complex challenge of long-term conversational memory in multi-party dialogues.
The system aims to go beyond simple content retrieval by tracking speaker identity, relational dynamics, and evolving group states.
It critiques existing general-purpose LLM memory systems for failing to maintain crucial person and group relations in complex conversations.

stories.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
stories.author: Jiantao Jiao
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Serve, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating AI agents in production inference engineering tasks.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which either lack inference focus (repo-level) or cover too few inference tasks (general terminal-agent benchmarks).
Highlights the complexity of production inference, requiring coordination across model support, runtime execution, and public APIs.

stories.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
stories.author: Xitong Gao
bullet_points: Addresses a key inefficiency in LLM agents: redundant control decision reconstruction within task contexts.
Introduces 'Growing Harness,' a training paradigm that aims to convert recurring control logic into reusable executable code.
Proposes reserving expensive LLM calls solely for task-specific semantic reasoning, improving efficiency.

stories.title: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It
stories.author: Junhao Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in type-safe decision models where output schema conformity does not guarantee correct semantic interpretation.
Researchers investigate how the assignment of option names to underlying rubrics affects the behavior of Jev-like typed decision models.
This research is relevant for applications where model outputs are consumed directly by software, requiring high reliability beyond mere structural correctness.

stories.title: FleXray: Universal Clinical X-ray Segmentation
stories.author: Neel Dey
bullet_points: FleXray addresses the challenge of segmenting structures in X-ray images, a modality known for its inherent 2D projection ambiguity.
The research tackles the difficulty of creating labeled X-ray datasets, which currently limits general-purpose morphometric analysis.
The development aims to enable more quantitative and broad functional analysis of X-ray data in clinical settings.

stories.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen
stories.author: Nick Rahimi
bullet_points: The study challenges the reliability of 'compile rate' as a metric for evaluating LLM-based code vulnerability repair.
Researchers conducted controlled experiments using three open-source LLMs (350M to 6.7B parameters) on real-world C/C++ vulnerabilities.
The paper proposes a 'change-aware screen' as a more scientifically robust evaluation method for patch quality.

stories.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows
stories.author: Augustus Griffin
bullet_points: The study investigates the practical time-saving potential of AI prompt-to-design workflows in digital product design.
It utilized a randomized controlled trial involving product designers and product managers to gather empirical data.
The research addresses the current gap in experimental evidence regarding AI's impact on product design workflows, contrasting with software engineering.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: Identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant, irrelevant proximal context overwhelms distant, crucial evidence.
Proposes LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) as a novel mechanism to mitigate this context interference.
Addresses a fundamental limitation in current long-context LLM research, moving beyond just distance-based challenges.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: Addresses the complex challenge of long-term memory in multi-party dialogue systems.
Highlights the limitations of current general-purpose LLM memory systems in tracking speaker roles and group dynamics.
Introduces 'SpeakerMem-R1,' a novel dual-track memory approach designed to preserve person and group relations during conversation.

stories.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
stories.author: En Yu
bullet_points: The paper identifies the 'Proximity Trap' in long-context LLMs, where abundant, irrelevant nearby context overwhelms distant, crucial evidence.
This challenges the prevailing assumption that context limitations are solely due to distance in long-context retrieval.
The authors propose LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment) to mitigate this trap using a t-distributed directional matching mechanism.

stories.title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning
stories.author: Jian Cheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses performance degradation in language models when using aggressive low-bit quantization (sub-3-bit).
Quantization-aware distillation (QAD) helps restore short-form QA performance but fails at complex mathematical and code reasoning.
The core issue identified is 'quantization-amplified exposure bias,' where errors compound during autoregressive generation.

stories.title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
stories.author: Angela Zhou
bullet_points: The research addresses challenges in Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE) for dynamic treatment rules using retrospective data.
It tackles the issue of annotating complex state/reward data (text/images) where expert labeling is costly.
The paper proposes an optimal sequential annotation strategy, potentially leveraging cheaper, imperfect classifiers alongside expert review.

stories.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
stories.author: Furu Wei
bullet_points: Introduces Agensh, a new scalable multi-agent harness designed to overcome limitations in current systems.
Agensh operates without a central orchestrator, allowing for concurrent execution of tasks by distributed workers.
The system aims to reduce latency in complex tasks by enabling self-organized multi-agent cooperation loops.

stories.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue
stories.author: Yingcai Wu
bullet_points: The paper introduces SpeakerMem-R1, a new memory system designed for multi-party dialogue.
It addresses the limitations of general LLM memory systems in tracking complex conversational dynamics.
Key challenges addressed include maintaining speaker identity, tracking relational states, and integrating distributed clues over long conversations.

stories.title: Measuring the Serving Stack Instead of the Model: Hidden Confounds in Local Tool-Use Evaluation
stories.author: Yuemeng Zheng
bullet_points: The study highlights that evaluating AI agent performance must account for the serving stack, not just the model itself.
Local serving environments (like Ollama) introduce hidden confounds that affect how agents emit valid tool calls.
Different models exhibit varying behaviors regarding tool invocation (e.g., text vs. native tool_calls) based on static serving configurations.

stories.title: Detecting GPT-Assisted Writing Using Interpretable Stylometric Features
stories.author: Alexander Fuchsberger
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical academic challenge of detecting AI-assisted writing (specifically GPT).
It evaluates the effectiveness of interpretable stylometric features extracted directly from text to distinguish authorship.
The study tested eight machine learning classifiers using a dataset of 90 participants who wrote both independently and with ChatGPT assistance.

stories.title: Diffusion Drafts, AR Verifies: Accelerating Document OCR with Self-Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Hongjoon Ahn
bullet_points: The research addresses the slow inference speed of autoregressive OCR vision-language models, which require sequential token decoding.
It proposes using diffusion-based parallel generation, which is promising because OCR outputs are grounded in the input image.
A key challenge identified is that predicting multiple tokens simultaneously in a diffusion step risks introducing errors because subsequent tokens are unknown during the initial prediction.

stories.title: Per-Agent Cost Tracking for Multi-Agent AI on AWS
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Addresses a critical, practical issue: tracking granular costs for multi-agent AI systems on AWS.
Highlights the danger of 'silent waste' where successful API calls (200 OK) still incur unexpected billing.
Provides a technical solution/insight for developers using AWS Bedrock and Strands crews to monitor resource consumption.

stories.title: AI Is Writing More of the Code — But Developers Are Becoming Responsible for More Than Ever
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: AI tools are increasingly capable of generating functional code.
The role of the developer is shifting from pure coding to oversight and responsibility.
The article discusses the increased accountability developers face as AI assists in development.
